findings.observation: Hypothetical release-candidate HTML contains noindex although the fictional brief says this service route should be public and indexable.

evidence.locator: Fictional fixture described in this example; no URL fetched
evidence.method: Authored hypothetical input, not a browser or crawler result
evidence.observation: Fictional initial HTML: <meta name="robots" content="noindex">. Intended production index policy is indexable.
evidence.limitations: Illustrates a decision only. No actual site, deployment or business was inspected.

findings.guidance_scope: Google index eligibility for an intended public route, not an instruction to remove staging protection

sources.supports: Google must be able to access indexable content; index eligibility does not guarantee indexing.
Removing initial noindex through JavaScript is unreliable because rendering can be skipped.

findings.impact: If this fixture described a real release, an intended landing page could remain excluded. No traffic loss is estimated.
findings.priority_reason: The fictional intended public route has a concrete index blocker; staging noindex is not itself a defect.
findings.confidence_reason: The supplied fictional HTML and fictional index intent conflict; production state and business impact are unmeasured.
findings.effort: About 1–2 hours after environment intent is confirmed; estimate only

assumptions: Fictional small site has separate environment configuration and an existing testable build; no deployment or access waiting included

dependencies: Confirm production versus staging index policy
Separate authorization to implement and later launch
findings.recommended_change: In an authorized implementation, separate production directives from staging controls; remove unintended production noindex at its generating layer. Preserve protected staging.
findings.validation: Check initial HTML and X-Robots-Tag for the production candidate; verify staging stays protected. Recheck actual production after authorized launch. Search Console indexing remains a separate later observation.
findings.rollback: Restore prior configuration/ref if routing or privacy regresses; release owner verifies staging protection. No change has been made.

findings.observation: No field performance data exists in this fictional input. A supposed lab score cannot establish a field pass.
findings.guidance_scope: Field performance measurement; no claim of current values or ranking effect

sources.section: Core Web Vitals and lab tools
sources.supports: Assess good LCP, INP and CLS at the 75th percentile by device; Lighthouse load tests do not measure field INP.

findings.impact: Real visitors could have good or poor performance; neither is established.
findings.priority_reason: A measurement gap needs an owner and plan, not an invented performance incident.
findings.confidence_reason: No field sample or actual lab result was supplied.
findings.effort: Estimate after authorized measurement options are known
dependencies: Authorized public launch and sufficient field data, or separately authorized private measurement
findings.recommended_change: Record a reproducible lab baseline before launch and review available field evidence afterward. Preserve unknown field status until data is sufficient.
findings.validation: Record source, collection window, device, page/origin scope and all three field values or explicit missing-data reasons. Do not convert TBT into INP or missing values into zero.
findings.rollback: Not applicable to this read-only investigation; any future instrumentation needs its own rollback plan.

findings.observation: The fictional business uses a private home address and has no owner-approved public storefront address. The proposed Google LocalBusiness rich-result implementation is ineligible as scoped.

evidence.locator: Fictional fixture described in this example; no URL fetched
evidence.method: Authored hypothetical input, not a browser or crawler result
evidence.observation: Fictional owner policy: service-area business; home address is private and must not be published.
evidence.limitations: Illustrates a decision only. No actual site, deployment or business was inspected.

findings.guidance_scope: Google LocalBusiness rich-result required fields; does not prohibit truthful Schema.org vocabulary use

sources.supports: Name and physical address are required for this Google feature.
Service-area businesses should hide their address from customers on the profile.

findings.impact: Preserves address privacy; no claim that the site is excluded from ordinary search.
findings.priority_reason: Resolve the proposed feature scope before implementation; privacy must not be traded for eligibility.
findings.confidence_reason: The hypothetical privacy constraint and documented required field conflict; no real business facts were gathered.
findings.owner: Business owner and content engineer (fictional roles)
findings.effort: About 30–60 minutes to document the decision; estimate only
dependencies: Verify which business facts are approved for publication
findings.recommended_change: Do not expose or invent an address. Omit this rich-result claim and consider only truthful applicable entity markup without suggesting it substitutes for required LocalBusiness fields.
findings.validation: Confirm no private address appears in visible content, JSON-LD, source, assets or public reports. Document the feature eligibility limitation and separately validate any included markup.
findings.rollback: If a future authorized change exposes private data, follow the incident/removal process and restore the safe version; no data has been published by this example.
